hook: Uppal gets a new bus terminal for *1 lakh* passengers a day, in 100 days
tldr: Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar laid the foundation for a ₹3.22 crore bus terminal at Uppal Zonal Workshop, promised in 100 days. TGSRTC is also converting 250 old diesel buses to electric.

beats.what: A new bus terminal at the Uppal Zonal Workshop, built for ₹3.22 crore, is meant to serve nearly one lakh passengers a day and be ready in 100 days.
beats.why: It's part of TGSRTC's clean-mobility push: 3,000 electric buses are already in the fleet, 2,200 more are coming under PM e-Drive, and 250 old diesel buses are being retrofitted as EVs.
beats.care: Commute via Uppal or east Hyderabad? Expect a proper terminal by early February, and more e-buses on your routes.

cards.body: The minister also said a committee with the newly elected recognised union will start the process of merging TGSRTC employees with the government, the workers' main demand.

cards.caption: old diesel buses being converted to electric (phase 1)
cards.body: Retrofitting is cheaper than buying new buses and cuts emissions.

cards.q: Would a better Uppal terminal get you to take the bus more?
opts: No, I prefer metro or bike

cards.q: How many electric buses are already in the TGSRTC fleet?
cards.why: 3,000 are already in; 2,200 more are coming under PM e-Drive.

learn.t: Retrofitting swaps a bus's diesel engine for an electric motor and batteries, keeping the body and chassis.

watch: Whether the terminal opens on time (around early February), and which routes get the retrofitted e-buses first.
